quote: The driver of a vehicle within an intersection intending to turn to the left shall yield the right-of-way to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction which is within the intersection or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard, but such driver, having so yielded and having given a signal when and as required, may make such left turn and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle making the left turn.

activation.condition: driver is within an intersection intending to turn left; an opposite-direction vehicle is within the intersection or sufficiently close to pose an immediate hazard

obligation.description: yield right-of-way to the qualifying opposite-direction vehicle before making the left turn

exceptions.trigger: subject has yielded and given a signal when and as required
exceptions.effect: subject may make the left turn
exceptions.replacement_obligation: other opposite-direction drivers approaching the intersection shall yield to the turning vehicle
exceptions.source_clause: but such driver, having so yielded and having given a signal when and as required, may make such left turn and the drivers of all other vehicles approaching the intersection from the opposite direction shall yield the right-of-way to the vehicle making the left turn.

timing.description: initial yield precedes the signalled turn; opposing duty follows the subject having yielded and making the turn

judgment_calls_needed.note: No numeric legal time-to-conflict threshold is supplied.
Signal sufficiency depends on other applicable signal rules and original context.
Observed body and speed histories do not by themselves decide legal priority.
